items.text: Adjusted swimming depth thresholds to start at 1.17 m and stop below 0.9 m, reducing animation dithering and slightly delaying exit from shallow water.
Car lifts now refuse to grab a car if any animals are mounted on it.
Fixed dismount action to properly remove the stir bar, preventing leftover objects after exiting.

Wool can be recycled into 5 cloth pieces; adult cows/sheep lifespan doubled to 48 h; livestock feeding now uses food calories (high‑calorie foods 6× more effective, low‑calorie less) and prevents eating spoiled produce; ranch sales now give 30‑50 high‑quality metal ore instead of HQM.
Milk products now provide double calories and triple hydration; beef and rich beef pies last 120 min (up from 30 min); mutton pie renamed to shepherd's pie and now requires a potato.
Spiral staircases now decay and count toward TC upkeep; added server‑population‑scaled settings for power‑plant heavy fuse decay rate.
Helipad repair now requires 30,000 wood, 10,000 metal fragments, and 100 rope, and added AIRWOLF CCTV (S2P).

Fixed armored triangle ladder hatch collision meshes, biofuel generator flag collision, and prevented composters from becoming bricked when splashed by water, restoring proper placement and functionality.
Improved client‑side prediction for thrown projectiles, reconciling position and velocity with server data and handling stick events reliably.
Machete network range reduced from medium to low, decreasing its effective reach in multiplayer.
Grenade drop animation now synchronized with throw release, ensuring grenades spawn at the intended moment.
Fish hitboxes corrected and death animation loops fixed, improving combat accuracy with critter animals.
Added ferry terminal and radtown locations.
Crate in Radtown moved and window sign replaced with a two‑sided variant to stop looting through the window gap.
Reapplied the NMS loot room after file conflicts, restoring its availability.
Shields and diving tanks now appear correctly in the backpack slot of the loadout screen.
Animals can no longer slip through doors at monuments, preventing unintended entry and protecting bases.

- Machete network range reduced from medium to low, decreasing its effective reach in multiplayer.

- Fish hitboxes corrected and death animation loops fixed, improving combat accuracy with critter animals.

### World, Map & Exploits
- Added ferry terminal and radtown locations.
- Crate in Radtown moved and window sign replaced with a two‑sided variant to stop looting through the window gap.
- Reapplied the NMS loot room after file conflicts, restoring its availability.

### Inventory & UI

### Gameplay & Balance
- Animals can no longer slip through doors at monuments, preventing unintended entry and protecting bases.

items.text: Sheep now drop the wool they were wearing at the moment of death.
Lambs no longer drop dung and sheep dung drop behavior fixed, aligning both with calf behavior.
Bad genes are now more common, making generic‑looking sheep and cows prevalent while rare good‑gene variants (e.g., black sheep) become harder to find.

Added a new mutton pie (regular and rich). Regular pie halves the time needed for livestock to reach the Bonded state; the rich version cuts an additional 30 seconds. The pie also prevents bulls from charging.

Added a new beef pie (regular and rich). Regular pie raises the maximum food calories a player can consume for a duration by 75 % (to 875 cal), increasing downed‑recovery chance to 75 % when the hunger bar is full. The rich version raises the cap to 1000 cal and guarantees 100 % recovery chance.
Mount prompt is hidden when no animal is being led. Mounting slots now specify supported animal size (large or small); cows no longer fit in the small flatbed and must use the large flatbed.
Fixed a crash scenario where the store could break when the player’s inventory was empty.
Fixed hair and eyebrows being incorrectly overridden and added support for a character slot in connection strings.
Sheep now drop the wool they were wearing at death.
Lambs no longer drop dung; sheep dung drop bug fixed.
Bad genes are now more common, making generic‑looking sheep and cows prevalent; good genes (e.g., black sheep) are rarer.
Collider sizes for livestock and critters adjusted, improving hit detection and interaction.
Sheep trophy head added to hunting trophies; male calf ragdoll display corrected for female bodies.
Regular and rich mutton pies halve livestock bonding time (rich reduces an extra 30 s) and prevent bulls from charging.
Regular and rich beef pies increase max food duration by 75 % (875 cal) and boost downed‑player recovery chance to 75 % (regular) or 100 % (rich) after hunger bar is full.
Ridable horse prefab added, allowing players to mount horses.
Boat power‑down fixed when lowering sails and jumping off quickly, preventing uncontrolled drifting.
Mounting UI improvements: prompt only appears when leading an animal, slots now indicate supported size, and cows require the large flatbed.
External gate upgrades now persist; deployables no longer clip through or disappear when doors close, and fuseboxes restored on all applicable monuments.

Deployable placement respects terrain deformation with configurable tolerance, foundations align to original terrain height, oil pumps now have a 15‑minute start delay (total 35 min cycle), and helipad repair stages affect functionality.
Store UI edge case fixed when player has no items.
Crafting menu overflow resolved by reducing category button width; mini crossbow fractional reload behavior corrected.
Computer station identifier input box text no longer disappears at various screen resolutions.
Sprint animation correctly stops when a networked attack is registered, fixing visual desync.
Loadout items now use proper container placement and older loadouts default to a safe position, fixing item placement bugs.
Hair and eyebrows customization now displays correctly, fixing overridden visuals.
Remote‑controlled turrets, drones and cameras ignore base occlusion, making them visible through walls (anti‑ESP).
Squirrel critters now move at adjusted speeds, changing how quickly they flee and can be harvested.
